problem_sources.text: About the Event: CTF 2026 is a hands-on Capture The Flag cybersecurity competition organized by the Digital Defence Club (DDC), Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology (CBIT). The competition is designed to provide students with practical exposure to cybersecurity through a series of problem-solving challenges based on real-world security concepts. The challenges will cover key cybersecurity domains including: Web Exploitation Cryptography Digital Forensics Reverse Engineering Network Security OSINT and related cybersecurity challenges The event aims to encourage hands-on learning, ethical hacking, technical problem-solving, teamwork, and practical cybersecurity skills among students. Eligibility: Open to college/university students from recognized institutions. Participants from different colleges are eligible to participate. Students from different specializations/branches are allowed to participate. Competition Format: The competition will consist of practical cybersecurity challenges across multiple categories, including: Web Exploitation Cryptography Digital Forensics Reverse Engineering Network Security Number of Challenges: The competition is expected to contain approximately 20–30 challenges across different cybersecurity categories. The exact number and difficulty of challenges may be modified by the organizers based on the final competition design. Duration: The competition is expected to run for approximately 2–3 hours. The exact schedule and timings will be communicated to registered participants before the event. Scoring: Each challenge will carry a predefined number of points. Participants/teams will receive points for successfully submitting correct flags. Higher-difficulty challenges may carry higher points. The leaderboard will be updated during the competition. In case of a tie, the earlier successful submission time may be used as a tie-breaker. Rules: Participants must register using their correct details. The competition is strictly for ethical and educational purposes. Participants must not attack or disrupt systems outside the designated CTF environment. Attacking the competition infrastructure, scoreboard, hosting server, or other participants' systems is prohibited. Participants must not share flags, solutions, or challenge answers during the competition. Any form of cheating, impersonation, plagiarism, or unauthorized collaboration may result in disqualification. Participants must not intentionally disrupt the competition or interfere with other participants. Organizers reserve the right to investigate suspicious activity and take appropriate action. Participants must follow all instructions provided by the organizers. The decision of the organizers regarding rule violations and disqualification will be final. Technical Requirements: Fully charged laptop Stable internet connectivity, where required Modern web browser Required cybersecurity tools/utilities as permitted by the organizers Participants are responsible for ensuring that their systems are ready before the competition begins. Participation Fee: A registration/participation fee of ₹100 per participant will be applicable. Food & Refreshments Lunch will be provided to registered participants during the event. Prizes & Recognition: Top-performing participants/teams may receive: Cash prizes / prizes as announced Certificates Winner recognition Additional rewards or goodies, subject to sponsorship and event arrangements Important Instructions: Participants must report to the venue before the scheduled competition time. Participants should carry valid college/student identification. Participants are expected to maintain professional and ethical conduct throughout the event. Any updates or changes to the event schedule will be communicated through official event channels. The organizers reserve the right to modify the challenge structure, timings, or rules if required for the smooth conduct of the competition.

raw.details:
About the Event:

  • CTF 2026 is a hands-on Capture The Flag cybersecurity competition organized by the Digital Defence Club (DDC), Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology (CBIT).
  • The competition is designed to provide students with practical exposure to cybersecurity through a series of problem-solving challenges based on real-world security concepts.

The challenges will cover key cybersecurity domains including:

  • Web Exploitation
  • Cryptography
  • Digital Forensics
  • Reverse Engineering
  • Network Security
  • OSINT and related cybersecurity challenges

The event aims to encourage hands-on learning, ethical hacking, technical problem-solving, teamwork, and practical cybersecurity skills among students.

Eligibility:

  • Open to college/university students from recognized institutions.
  • Participants from different colleges are eligible to participate.
  • Students from different specializations/branches are allowed to participate.

Competition Format:

  • The competition will consist of practical cybersecurity challenges across multiple categories, including:
  • Web Exploitation
  • Cryptography
  • Digital Forensics
  • Reverse Engineering
  • Network Security

Number of Challenges:

  • The competition is expected to contain approximately 20–30 challenges across different cybersecurity categories.
  • The exact number and difficulty of challenges may be modified by the organizers based on the final competition design.

Duration:

  • The competition is expected to run for approximately 2–3 hours.
  • The exact schedule and timings will be communicated to registered participants before the event.

Scoring:

  • Each challenge will carry a predefined number of points.
  • Participants/teams will receive points for successfully submitting correct flags.
  • Higher-difficulty challenges may carry higher points.
  • The leaderboard will be updated during the competition.
  • In case of a tie, the earlier successful submission time may be used as a tie-breaker.

Rules:

  • Participants must register using their correct details.
  • The competition is strictly for ethical and educational purposes.
  • Participants must not attack or disrupt systems outside the designated CTF environment.
  • Attacking the competition infrastructure, scoreboard, hosting server, or other participants' systems is prohibited.
  • Participants must not share flags, solutions, or challenge answers during the competition.
  • Any form of cheating, impersonation, plagiarism, or unauthorized collaboration may result in disqualification.
  • Participants must not intentionally disrupt the competition or interfere with other participants.
  • Organizers reserve the right to investigate suspicious activity and take appropriate action.
  • Participants must follow all instructions provided by the organizers.
  • The decision of the organizers regarding rule violations and disqualification will be final.

Technical Requirements:

  • Fully charged laptop
  • Stable internet connectivity, where required
  • Modern web browser
  • Required cybersecurity tools/utilities as permitted by the organizers
  • Participants are responsible for ensuring that their systems are ready before the competition begins.

Participation Fee:

  • A registration/participation fee of ₹100 per participant will be applicable.
  • Food & Refreshments
  • Lunch will be provided to registered participants during the event.

Prizes & Recognition:

  • Top-performing participants/teams may receive:
  • Cash prizes / prizes as announced
  • Certificates
  • Winner recognition
  • Additional rewards or goodies, subject to sponsorship and event arrangements

Important Instructions:

  • Participants must report to the venue before the scheduled competition time.
  • Participants should carry valid college/student identification.
  • Participants are expected to maintain professional and ethical conduct throughout the event.
  • Any updates or changes to the event schedule will be communicated through official event channels.
  • The organizers reserve the right to modify the challenge structure, timings, or rules if required for the smooth conduct of the competition.
